newsitem.title: PERU: Lima shares edge to higher close in low volume.
newsitem.headline: Lima shares edge to higher close in low volume.

text.p: Shares on the Lima stock exchange closed up Friday in low volume as investors cautiously awaited first-quarter financial results news to filter into the market next week, brokers said.
Companies were not due to publish their official results until next month, but rumors of the financial statements were likely to swirl around the exchange next week, they added.
Friday, the General Index rose 0.26 percent to 1,731.28 points, while the blue-chip Selective Index climbed 0.41 percent to 2,509.46 points.
In a total of 1,546 trades, volume was a meager 24.7 million soles ($9.3 million), according to preliminary figures. Brokers said they expected a mixed market Monday based on speculative investments.
The most notable trade Friday centered on chocolate maker D'Onofrio, which rose 8.73 percent to 1.37 soles on volume of 129,000 shares.

The gain was due to rumors that D'Onofrio's new owner, Switzerland's Nestle SA, which earlier this month bought 98.7 percent of the company's common shares, also planned an offer for its more liquid labor shares.
"D'Onofrio climbed because of rumors that Nestle will make a public offer for its labor shares," Jose Cervantes of local brokerage Investa said.
Backus y Johnston, the country's top brewery, remained stable closing at 2.30 soles in volume of 681,000 shares.
Benchmark Telefonica del Peru saw little trade as it rose 1.10 percent to 6.46 soles in volume of 407,000 shares.
"The market is cautious due to speculation. Some players think certian companies will rise, while others believe the same ones will fall," Luis Cueva of Argos said.
